title: Denmark-England
capsule: The union of Denmark and England refers to the North Sea empire assembled by Cnut the Great, who conquered England in 1016 after years of campaigning alongside his father Sweyn Forkbeard, then inherited Denmark in 1018 and acquired Norway by 1028. Cnut ruled England through a sophisticated administrative system, issued law codes, and was accepted by the English church and nobility as a legitimate Christian king, even attending the coronation of Holy Roman Emperor Conrad II in Rome in 1027. The union dissolved rapidly after Cnut's death in 1035: his sons Harold Harefoot and Harthacnut divided the realm and ruled briefly in succession, and in 1042 the English nobility recalled the Anglo-Saxon claimant Edward the Confessor, ending Scandinavian rule in England.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political union's extent over England and Denmark is historically well established; exact subordinate administrative boundaries and Norway's integration degree are less precisely documented.
